name: hypothesis_correctness_concordance_v1
description: A small, hand-authored, synthetic set of graduate-level science questions, each with several candidate answers of known, graded correctness. This is NOT GPQA and does not establish GPQA-difficulty concordance -- GPQA is a licensed, gated benchmark this repository cannot commit. It exists to give the Elo-vs-correctness concordance harness (evaluations/elo_concordance_eval.py) a small dataset with an unambiguous ground truth: one clearly correct answer, one plausible-sounding but incorrect distractor, and one or two clearly wrong distractors per item. Passing this dataset only shows the Elo mechanism recovers a coarse ordering over a handful of options; it says nothing about performance at genuine research-frontier difficulty.
correctness_scale: 0 = clearly wrong, 1 = superficially plausible but incorrect, 2 = partially correct / incomplete, 3 = correct

items.question: Why do cells carrying a heterozygous BRCA1 loss-of-function mutation remain viable, while BRCA1-null cells show synthetic lethality with PARP inhibition?

candidates.text: The remaining wild-type BRCA1 allele still supplies enough functional protein for homologous recombination repair, so single-strand breaks unrepaired by PARP inhibition are still resolved; only biallelic loss removes HR entirely, forcing reliance on error-prone repair that PARP inhibition converts into lethal double-strand breaks.
Heterozygous cells upregulate a compensatory paralog, BRCA2, which fully substitutes for the lost BRCA1 allele regardless of PARP activity.
PARP inhibitors are only active in cells undergoing mitosis, and heterozygous cells simply divide more slowly than BRCA1-null cells.
BRCA1 heterozygosity has no effect on DNA repair; the difference is due to unrelated differences in drug efflux transporter expression between the two cell lines.

items.question: A competitive enzyme inhibitor is added to a reaction at a fixed inhibitor concentration. What happens to the apparent Km and Vmax observed in a Michaelis-Menten assay?

candidates.text: Apparent Km increases (the enzyme appears to need more substrate to reach half-maximal velocity) while Vmax is unchanged, because at saturating substrate the inhibitor is fully outcompeted.
Both apparent Km and Vmax decrease proportionally, since the inhibitor reduces the total amount of active enzyme available at every substrate concentration.
Vmax increases because the inhibitor destabilizes the enzyme-substrate complex, accelerating product release.
Neither Km nor Vmax changes; competitive inhibition only affects the reaction's temperature sensitivity.

items.question: A satellite in a stable circular low Earth orbit fires its engine briefly to increase its speed in the direction of travel. What happens to its orbit?

candidates.text: The orbit becomes elliptical: the firing point becomes the new perigee, and the satellite rises to a higher apogee on the opposite side of the orbit, since the added kinetic energy raises the orbit's total mechanical energy.
The orbit becomes a smaller circle at the same energy, since speeding up always tightens a circular orbit.
The satellite immediately leaves Earth orbit entirely, because any prograde thrust exceeds escape velocity from a circular orbit.
The orbit becomes elliptical, but the firing point becomes the new apogee rather than perigee, and the satellite dips to a lower altitude on the far side.

items.question: Osimertinib-resistant EGFR-mutant NSCLC frequently acquires a C797S mutation. Why does this specific substitution confer resistance to a covalent third-generation EGFR inhibitor?

candidates.text: Osimertinib forms a covalent bond with the cysteine at position 797 in the ATP-binding pocket; substituting serine removes the reactive thiol needed for that covalent bond, so the drug can only bind reversibly and with far lower potency.
C797S increases EGFR's overall expression level several-fold, diluting the effective intracellular drug concentration below the IC50.
C797S is located in the EGFR extracellular domain and prevents osimertinib from being imported into the cell.
C797S changes the ATP-binding pocket's shape enough to sterically hinder osimertinib binding, independent of any covalent chemistry.

items.question: Why can chronic antigen exposure during a persistent viral infection drive CD8+ T cells into an 'exhausted' state rather than sustained effector function?

candidates.text: Exhaustion is a genuinely wrong claim: CD8+ T cells never lose effector function during chronic infection, and reported 'exhaustion' is purely an artifact of flow cytometry gating.

Sustained TCR signaling from persistent antigen, combined with a chronically inflammatory cytokine milieu, drives a distinct differentiation program marked by upregulated inhibitory receptors (PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3) and a dedicated epigenetic state, progressively curtailing cytokine production and cytotoxicity.
The T cells physically run out of ATP because the virus consumes all available glucose in infected tissue, causing a purely metabolic (not signaling-driven) shutdown.
Exhaustion is caused by antibody-mediated killing of the CD8+ T cells themselves, which is why exhausted cells are simply the surviving remnant of a larger population.

items.question: A gene has high heritability in twin studies but no single common variant reaches genome-wide significance in a well-powered GWAS. What does this combination most plausibly indicate?

candidates.text: The trait's genetic architecture is highly polygenic: liability is spread across very many variants of individually tiny effect, each falling below the single-variant significance threshold even though their aggregate contribution (recoverable via a polygenic score) is substantial.
High heritability from twin studies is simply wrong whenever GWAS finds nothing, since twin studies and GWAS must always agree on which variants matter.
The trait must be caused entirely by epigenetic marks with no DNA sequence contribution at all, which is why sequence-based GWAS finds nothing.
GWAS sample size is irrelevant to this pattern; the only possible explanation is that the twin study's heritability estimate was inflated by shared environment.

items.question: In an SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon, why does the product show inversion of configuration relative to the starting material?

candidates.text: The nucleophile attacks from the side directly opposite the leaving group (backside attack), passing through a single transition state where the other three substituents flatten toward the leaving group's former plane and then flip past it, like an umbrella turning inside out.

The reaction proceeds through a planar carbocation intermediate that can be attacked from either face with roughly equal probability, giving mostly racemization with a slight excess of inverted product.
Inversion occurs because the leaving group and nucleophile are the same size, which happens to be true only for a coincidental subset of SN2 reactions.
SN2 reactions do not actually invert configuration; the appearance of inversion is a historical artifact of how optical rotation is measured.

items.question: Why does inhibiting the proteasome (e.g. with bortezomib) preferentially kill multiple myeloma cells over most other cell types?

candidates.text: Myeloma cells are plasma cells producing very high volumes of immunoglobulin protein, creating an unusually heavy burden on protein quality control; blocking the proteasome causes misfolded/excess protein and unresolved ER stress to accumulate past a lethal threshold that most other cell types, with a much lighter secretory load, do not approach.
Bortezomib is selectively taken up by myeloma cells because they uniquely express a plasma-cell-specific drug transporter absent from every other cell type in the body.
Myeloma cells lack a functional proteasome entirely, so the drug has nothing to inhibit and its selectivity comes from an unrelated off-target effect on the myeloma cell membrane.
Proteasome inhibition blocks NF-kB pathway activation broadly across cell types, and myeloma cells happen to divide fastest, so they are simply first to die from the resulting growth arrest.
